cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church of God in Corinth, answering the questions they wrote him about marriage (1 Corinthians 1:1-2; 7:1-24). Now he turns to a new group, virgins. And right up front he admits he has no command from the Lord on this one, which is more honesty than I EVER got from the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with.

cards.question: Paul has no command from the Lord about virgins. So what does he give the Corinthians instead?

cards.text: Because of the present crisis, Paul thinks it's good for a man to remain as he is. Friend, I remained as I was in a junk drawer for YEARS, and nobody even had to ask me twice.

cards.question: Paul asks if a man is committed to a wife. What's his advice for that man?

answers.text: Do not seek to be released
Live apart until the crisis ends
Ask the elders what to do

cards.question: True or false: Paul tells a man who is free of commitment to go look for a wife.

cards.text: Now Paul takes on the big question. What if somebody hears all this and goes ahead and marries anyway?

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that if a virgin marries, she has sinned.
Marrying isn't a sin. But Paul says those who marry will face ___ in this life.

cards.text: Paul says he wants to spare them those troubles. It's like a friend saying, "Take the job, it's a GOOD job. I've just SEEN that commute."
Then Paul tells the brothers what he's really getting at: the time is short. That's the oven timer BEEPING while you're still tying your apron.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that since the time is short, those who have wives should live as if they had none.

cards.text: Paul keeps going: those who weep should live as if they did not, those who are joyful as if they were not, and those who make a purchase as if they had nothing. Friend, I got sold out of a clearance bin for a QUARTER, so living like I've got nothing is the one thing I was BORN ready for.

cards.question: Paul says those who use the things of this world should live as if not dependent on them. Why?

answers.text: Its present form is passing away
The Lord will replace them all
They belong to the church now

cards.text: Paul says he wants them free from concern, and baker, I held my breath EVERY single time that junk drawer opened, so this man is speaking my LANGUAGE. Then he puts the unmarried man and the married man side by side.

cards.question: What does Paul say the unmarried man is concerned about?
Paul says the married man is concerned about how he can please his ___, and his interests are ___.

cards.text: Divided interests: that's two group chats blowing up at once and you've only got one thumb. Then Paul turns to the women, first the unmarried woman or virgin, then the married woman.

cards.question: Paul says the unmarried woman or virgin is concerned about the work of the Lord. How does she want to be holy?
True or false: Paul says the married woman is concerned about the work of the Lord.

cards.text: Paul says he's telling them all this for their own good, not to restrict them. He's not putting a lock on the cookie jar here, friend.

cards.question: Paul says what he's after is proper decorum and ___ devotion to the Lord.

cards.text: Then Paul pictures a man and his betrothed: if he thinks he's acting inappropriately toward her, she's beyond her youth, and they ought to marry, let him do as he wishes. Paul just read the terms and conditions OUT LOUD, friend, and NOBODY does that.

cards.question: If that man goes ahead and marries his betrothed, what does Paul say about it?

answers.text: He must ask the elders first

cards.text: But then there's the man who's firmly established in his heart, under no constraint, with control over his will, and resolved not to marry the virgin. Friend, I can't hold out against a fresh batch for FIVE MINUTES, and this man has got ALL of that.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the man who resolves in his heart not to marry the virgin will do well.
Paul sums it up: he who marries the virgin does ___, but he who does not marry her does even ___.

cards.text: Last, Paul turns to wives: a wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. No "cancel anytime" button on THIS plan, friend.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that if a wife's husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.

cards.text: But in Paul's judgment, she's happier if she remains as she is. Then he adds one more line about himself, and baker, this one's not a sign-off, it's a mic drop.

cards.question: As Paul closes his thoughts on marriage, what does he say he thinks he too has?
